object.medium: Acoustic 78 rpm gramophone recording; a thumri in raga Gara
object.description: On 8 November 1902, in a Calcutta hotel room, Gauhar Jaan sang into Fred Gaisberg's horn and ended with the words 'My name is Gauhar Jaan': the first recording made in India by an Indian artist. Two years later the Gramophone Company came back and recorded her again; this thumri in raga Gara is from that 1904 session. She was the subcontinent's first gramophone star, cut some six hundred sides in a dozen languages, charged three thousand rupees a session and toured in a carriage with a retinue. Before her, a performance in Calcutta ended when the singer stopped. After her, it could be heard in Madras, in London, and a hundred and twenty years later here. The piece is 'Aan baan jiya mein lago'.
facts: The 1902 sessions used wax masters shipped to Hanover for pressing; the first Indian discs went on sale in 1903.
She recorded in Hindustani, Bengali, Persian, Arabic, English and more, usually ending with her spoken name so the Hanover engineers could label the record.
Her thumri style, light-classical and emotional, was the gramophone's first Indian idiom.
